newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Banks queue to lend MPT cash for HK Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: Banks queue to lend MPT cash for HK Telecom stake.

text.p: Banks were queueing up to lend China Telecom (Hong Kong) funds to help pay for its purchase of 5.5 percent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, finance indsutry sources said on Monday.

Banks were bidding for a mandate to arrange a loan for China Telecom, which earlier this month agreed to pay Cable & Wireless Plc HK$14.25 a share or a total of HK$9.177 billion for 5.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom, they said.
"We want to be involved," said one senior banker.
"The industry is an industry which has no credit problems. Telecoms are a very strong and robust industry," he added, predicting a loan of about US$800 million.
Banks predicted the deal would resemble the fundraising by a unit of China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd, which has taken a 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom.
China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd, controlled by China's State Council, said earlier this month that a unit had signed a US$1.05 billion loan to part-finance its Hongkong Telecom stake.
The unit had earlier agreed to pay HK$12.60 a share or a total of HK$11.4 billion for 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd.
China Telecom is indirectly controlled by Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, China's largest telecom provider.
China Everbright is one of 16 equal shareholders in China United Telecommunications Corp (China Unicom), China's second largest telecom provider and a rival of MPT.
